subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should it be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or folded into broader egress policy?
rationale: This changes an SSRF boundary and public config contract; the lower-level primitive exists, but the safe API shape, authorization model, and hard-deny behavior require maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped Nested SSRF Policy
options.body: Add a default-off `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` capability with explicit dangerous naming, metadata/link-local rules, cache isolation, redirect checks, audit output, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Design
options.body: Pause this specific flag and resolve it through the broader web-tool allow/deny egress policy tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685.

options.title: Keep Arbitrary Private Fetch Blocked
options.body: Leave current main limited to narrow fake-IP/proxy opt-ins and document that arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` is intentionally unsupported for now.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Nested SSRF Policy
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` capability with explicit dangerous naming, metadata/link-local rules, cache isolation, redirect checks, audit output, docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible policy-review signal and recent history across the SSRF, guarded-fetch, and web_fetch surfaces involved in this boundary choice.
